userStories.title: Display pending approval for three web actions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Keep ticket creation, fleet cancellation and thread send pending until the returned response represents an executed write.

**Motivation** — People can see success for a write still awaiting approval, lose access to usable thread controls, or see an acknowledged cancellation finish as completed.

**Approach** — Finding 10. ApprovalPendingFilter returns HTTP 202 with an enveloped ApprovalRequestSummaryDto. Ticket submit currently ignores the result, fleet cancel assigns it to the job view, and thread send merges it as a message. Distinguish the approval summary using its actual shape in the request/response path. Limit the behavior change to these three operations. Expose the returned request ID and keep the draft or job visible. Translate new copy in both locales. Preserve the existing retry rules for transport errors and closing sessions.

For the three approval-gated web calls, use the existing unwrapped approval summary. Check the operation's permission key, pending status and request ID, following the existing fleet dispatch UI. A pending transcript message also has a pending status. A queued reindex also has HTTP status 202. Neither alone identifies an approval.

**Scope** — In: extend useApi.ts, useFleetJobs.ts, CreateTicketDialog.vue, the project fleet-job detail page, thread-controller.ts, ThreadComposer.vue and both thread-detail page adapters; add en/zh feedback and extend their existing package tests. Out: stream catch-up and snapshot ordering (US-002), project load states (US-003), send permission decisions (US-005), and unrelated approval-gated operations. Changes to the public approval wire format, permission catalog or fleet protocol. Create no new files.

**Interface** — Reuse ApprovalRequestSummary from lib/approval-requests.ts and the FleetJobOpenItems scoped pending pattern. The exact operation keys are ticket.create, fleet.job.cancel and thread.message.send. Widen cancellation and send result contracts only where needed; carry the pending request ID through the existing ThreadActionResult/page/composer chain without classifying it as executed success or transport failure. Executed cancellation still applies the returned job using the existing label-preserving path. Pending send removes only its own optimistic echo and retains the editable draft.

**Verification** — Extend tests/components/CreateTicketDialog.spec.ts, tests/pages/fleet-job-detail.spec.ts, tests/lib/thread-controller.spec.ts, tests/components/thread-composer.spec.ts, tests/pages/threads-detail-actions-page.spec.ts and tests/composables/useApi.spec.ts. Mount the real composer through the project action page; use actual unwrapped summary fixtures, not a made-up pending marker. Dated review fixtures are read-only.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] When the mounted ticket-create action receives an ApprovalRequestSummary with permissionKey 'ticket.create', status 'pending' and a returned request ID, it displays pending feedback containing that ID.

[integration] When the mounted job-cancel action receives an ApprovalRequestSummary with permissionKey 'fleet.job.cancel', status 'pending' and a returned request ID, it displays pending feedback containing that ID.

[integration] When the mounted thread-send action receives an ApprovalRequestSummary with permissionKey 'thread.message.send', status 'pending' and a returned request ID, it displays pending feedback containing that ID.
[integration] When ticket submission awaits approval, CreateTicketDialog remains open with its populated form.
[integration] When ticket submission awaits approval, CreateTicketDialog emits no created event.
[integration] When a ticket-create or job-cancel response is pending approval, its mounted action produces zero execution-success toasts.
[integration] When cancellation awaits approval, the mounted fleet-job detail page continues to render the original job.
[integration] When thread send awaits approval, the mounted composer retains an editable draft.
[integration] When thread send awaits approval, the transcript returns to its pre-submit messages.
[unit] When createThreadController.send receives a pending approval response, it makes exactly one POST.
[integration] When the mounted ticket form receives the existing executed create response, it emits created.
[integration] When the mounted cancellation form receives the existing executed cancellation response, it renders the returned job.
[integration] When the mounted thread composer receives the existing executed send response, the returned message replaces its optimistic message.

userStories.title: Catch up when the thread event stream first becomes ready
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recover the initial GET-to-subscription gap and prevent stale thread snapshots from undoing live progress.

**Motivation** — People can see success for a write still awaiting approval, lose access to usable thread controls, or see an acknowledged cancellation finish as completed.

**Approach** — Finding 11. useThread and useWorkspaceThread both load before subscribing. createThreadEventStream marks the initial ready event live, while its resync callback currently fires on transport reopen. Catch up at server readiness once per connected stream, including reconnect. Reconcile thread detail and messages. Protect both snapshot ordering and updates to the same message sequence, including text deltas. A rejected background read must be handled and allow subsequent recovery.

**Scope** — In: extend lib/thread-event-stream.ts, lib/thread-controller.ts and lib/thread-view.ts and exercise both existing adapters. Preserve US-001 pending-send and optimistic-state behavior. Out: the project page's explicit load-error presentation/retry UI (US-003), list paging (US-004) and composer permission resolution (US-005). Create no new files.

**Interface** — Retain ThreadEventHandlers and the shared controller entry points. onResync must signal catch-up at ready, not independently at both transport open and ready. A connection includes the native EventSource reconnect path; duplicate ready frames do not create duplicate catch-ups. Reconcile detail as well as messages, and guard responses against later reads, same-sequence terminal updates, text deltas and teardown. Catch rejected fire-and-forget reads so a later connection can recover. Preserve stream dedupe, auth refresh/backoff and polling fallback.

**Verification** — Extend tests/lib/thread-event-stream.spec.ts, thread-event-stream-recovery.spec.ts and thread-controller.spec.ts plus tests/composables/useThread.spec.ts and useWorkspaceThread.spec.ts. Hold promises around ready and live events, including completion between initial GET and subscription in both scopes; stop during a held recovery to verify no reopened stream or poll. Dated event-bus fixtures are references only.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given either a project or workspace thread whose turn finishes between initial GET and subscription, when ready arrives without a disconnect, the controller reconciles the final transcript.
[integration] Given either scope whose turn finishes between initial GET and subscription, when ready arrives without a disconnect, the mounted composer becomes available.
[unit] When createThreadEventStream receives open, ready and duplicate ready, then reconnect open and ready, it initiates exactly one catch-up for each ready connection.

[unit] Given a held catch-up snapshot and either a newer onMessage-triggered read returning a terminal message or an onDelta text update for that same message sequence, when the older snapshot resolves, the message retains the status observed immediately before that response rather than regressing it.

[unit] Given a held catch-up snapshot and either a newer onMessage-triggered read returning a terminal message or an onDelta text update for that same message sequence, when the older snapshot resolves, the message retains its latest content.

[unit] Given a held catch-up snapshot and either a newer onMessage-triggered read returning a terminal message or an onDelta text update for that same message sequence, when the older snapshot resolves, the transcript contains exactly one copy of that message.
[unit] When a ready-triggered read rejects and a later reconnect succeeds, the thread controller recovers the transcript.
[unit] When the controller stops during a held recovery, completion of that recovery cannot reopen its stream.
[unit] When the controller stops during a held recovery, completion of that recovery cannot restart polling.

userStories.title: Show project thread errors and retry transient loads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give project-thread deep links explicit loading, unavailable and retryable states that clear when the thread recovers.

**Motivation** — People can see success for a write still awaiting approval, lose access to usable thread controls, or see an acknowledged cancellation finish as completed.

**Approach** — Finding 12. useThread suppresses its initial load rejection to keep the stream alive. Expose load state to the project detail page following useWorkspaceThread. Distinguish initial loading, unavailable or inaccessible detail and a retryable failure. Avoid revealing whether a forbidden thread exists. A successful retry or live recovery clears obsolete feedback.

**Scope** — In: extend composables/useThread.ts, pages/[project]/threads/[id].vue and both locale files when existing copy cannot be reused. Consume US-002 recovery without a second subscription. Out: stream reconciliation algorithms (US-002), thread list paging (US-004) and effective send grants (US-005). Preserve US-001 pending-send presentation. Create no new files.

**Interface** — Adapt the workspace loadFailed/loadThread pattern to expose project load state and a visible retry. A 403 and 404 have the same localized unavailable presentation and expose no private thread content; a transient 503 has a retry action. Retain mount/unmount guards and the single existing stream even after a failed initial GET. A valid thread obtained from a later live read must supersede the failed state, not remain masked by it.

**Verification** — Extend tests/pages/threads-detail-page.spec.ts and tests/composables/useThread.spec.ts with 403/404/503, explicit retry, live recovery and unmount. Use the existing mounted page and adapter harnesses; do not modify dated review fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] When a project-thread deep link returns 403 or 404, its detail area renders the same localized unavailable message for either response.
[integration] When a project-thread deep link returns 403 or 404, the detail area displays no private thread content.
[integration] Given an initial project-thread 503, when the user selects the visible retry action and the API returns valid detail, the page displays that thread.
[integration] Given an initial project-thread 503 followed by a successful visible retry, the page clears its obsolete failure feedback.
[integration] Given an initial project-thread 503 followed by a successful visible retry, the page uses exactly one thread subscription.
[unit] Given an initial load failure, when a later live reload resolves with a valid thread, stale error state no longer masks the loaded thread.

userStories.title: Page active and archived project threads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make project threads beyond the first 100 reachable for both statuses without corrupting the list during overlapping requests.

**Motivation** — People can see success for a write still awaiting approval, lose access to usable thread controls, or see an acknowledged cancellation finish as completed.

**Approach** — Finding 13. useThreads loads the first 100 rows for a status. Mirror useWorkspaceThreads' loadMore behavior on the project route. Retain the current generation guard across status switches and same-status reloads. Keep the page number on failure so retry reads the missing page.

**Scope** — In: extend composables/useThreads.ts, pages/[project]/threads/index.vue, tests/composables/useThreads.spec.ts and tests/pages/threads-page.spec.ts. Reuse existing localized load-more/retry controls and workspace paging conventions. Out: detail stream recovery (US-002/003), composer access (US-005) and API pagination contract changes. Create no new files.

**Interface** — Mirror useWorkspaceThreads current/hasNext/loadingMore/loadMore behavior for GET /projects/:slug/threads. Keep the selected status in every later-page request, retain existing page-one query behavior, append only successful current-generation pages, and leave the page counter unchanged on failure. Reject duplicate in-flight loadMore calls. Preserve both the composable generation and the page's independent guard around thread and member reads; a status switch or same-status reload invalidates older append responses.

**Verification** — Mount 101 ACTIVE and 101 ARCHIVED rows and exercise the actual load-more control. Use deferred page-two reads to cover status switches and same-status page-one reloads, plus double-click and retry of the same failed page with existing rows retained.

userStories.title: Apply effective project send permission to the composer
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enable project-thread input from effective any-row or own-row send grants rather than creator identity alone.

**Motivation** — People can see success for a write still awaiting approval, lose access to usable thread controls, or see an acknowledged cancellation finish as completed.

**Approach** — Finding 14. composerState gates on creator identity before checking sendRefusal and running messages. On the project page resolve send access from useProjectPermissions, including any-row and own-row keys and thread ownership. Pass the boolean into the shared composer logic. The workspace page supplies its existing personal-thread decision. Permissions still load asynchronously and API authorization remains authoritative.

**Scope** — In: change lib/thread-view.ts and both thread-detail pages; update tests/lib/thread-view.spec.ts, tests/pages/threads-detail-page.spec.ts, threads-detail-actions-page.spec.ts and workspace-thread-detail-page.spec.ts. Retain US-001 pending draft behavior and US-003 load/error states. Out: other creator/requester-based thread controls, API authorization changes, permission catalog changes and stream algorithms (US-002). Create no new files.

**Interface** — Replace the shared helper's creator-only send input with a resolved boolean. The project page reactively resolves permissions.value.has('thread.message.send') OR (isCreator AND permissions.value.hasOwn('thread.message.send')); useProjectPermissions already fails closed while loading or failed. Preserve sendRefusal and running-message reasons after access is granted. The personal workspace page supplies its existing owner-based decision and does not require project permissions for its composer. API refusals still surface through existing extractApiError behavior.

**Verification** — Mount real composer controls across any-row, own-row, absent and loading grants for creator and noncreator threads. Supply thread.message.send.own alongside thread.archive in the existing creator actions-page fixture, retaining typing, submission and refusal-toast assertions. userStories.title: Honor RUN cancellation through log drain
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make accepted RUN cancellation and the durable upload cutoff agree with the terminal event and command acknowledgement.

**Motivation** — People can see success for a write still awaiting approval, lose access to usable thread controls, or see an acknowledged cancellation finish as completed.

**Approach** — Finding 8. JobRun.finish computes a verdict before awaitLogs. For a RUN, serialize the final cancellation check with the RUNNING to UPLOADING journal transition. An accepted cancellation wins while the drain is held. A newly delivered cancellation after this cutoff must report refusal. Replay of an already handled command uses its recorded acknowledgement. Preserve command-specific CONFIG result semantics, existing lease fencing and recovery.

**Scope** — In: modify src/supervisor/job-run.ts, supervisor.ts and command-handler.ts plus job-run.spec.ts, supervisor.spec.ts and command-handler.spec.ts. Out: THREAD shutdown (US-007), changing API cancel/wire contracts, new lease rules, and redefining CONFIG's authoritative result precedence. Create no new files.

**Interface** — Propagate the active RUN requestCancel decision through Supervisor.cancel into CommandHandler's recorded acknowledgement. Use the same cutoff for a journal-only RUN before READOPT: RUNNING accepts durably; UPLOADING and terminal rows refuse a newly delivered CANCEL without mutating the journal. Serialize the post-drain durable cancellation check and RUNNING → UPLOADING transition through the existing journal transaction/state machinery without an intervening await. A resumed finish reads an already persisted cancellation. Previously recorded command IDs replay their recorded result even after the job ends; a different command ID is a fresh decision. Preserve single-terminal publication, upload fencing, epoch isolation, non-RUN behavior and existing CONFIG controls.

**Verification** — Drive ASSIGN and CANCEL through the real handler, Supervisor and SQLite Journal using the existing FakeExecutor/FakeLogShipping and injected clock seams. Hold drain after a successful RUN result, verify the durable timestamp and ok ack, then release it. Cover replay versus a distinct late command, journal-only restart before readoption, finish recovery and the existing job-run-config.spec.ts precedence control. Dated lifecycle fixtures are read-only.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given a RUN assigned through the handler and journal with a successful result and held log drain, when CANCEL is delivered, its acknowledgement is ok.
[integration] Given that RUN while log drain is held, when CANCEL is accepted, cancelRequestedAt is durable in the journal.
[integration] Given an accepted CANCEL during a successful RUN's held log drain, when drain is released, the runner publishes exactly one CANCELLED terminal event.
[integration] Given the same accepted CANCEL command ID, when it is replayed after completion, the handler returns its original acknowledgement.
[integration] Given the accepted CANCEL command ID replayed after completion, the run still has exactly one terminal event.
[integration] Given a previously uncancelled RUN in UPLOADING, when a distinct CANCEL is first delivered, the handler refuses it.
[integration] Given a previously uncancelled RUN in UPLOADING, when a distinct CANCEL is first delivered, cancelRequestedAt remains unset.
[unit] Given a persisted RUN with an accepted cancellation, when finish resumes, its final event is CANCELLED.
[unit] Given an otherwise identical successful RUN without cancellation, when finish resumes, its final event is COMPLETED.
[unit] Given restart before readoption and a journal-only RUNNING RUN, when a fresh CANCEL arrives, the journal records the cancellation request.
[unit] Given restart before readoption and a journal-only UPLOADING or terminal RUN, when a fresh CANCEL arrives, it is refused without changing the journal.

[unit] Given a CONFIG operation that already produced its authoritative result, when late cancellation arrives, its terminal state and reason still follow that result: COMPLETED for ok, no_changes or drift and FAILED for conflict, invalid, push_failed, pr_failed or timeout, with reason equal to the result outcome rather than CANCELLED, preserving existing late-cancel precedence.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module command replay, durable state and asynchronous drain require concurrency regressions; no authentication or credential behavior is changed.

userStories.title: Bound thread turn settlement and session close
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Bound THREAD shutdown across turn finalization and session close while making terminal stream sealing irreversible.

**Motivation** — People can see success for a write still awaiting approval, lose access to usable thread controls, or see an acknowledged cancellation finish as completed.

**Approach** — Finding 9. ThreadJobRun.finishRun awaits turnSettled before closeHeldSession starts its timed wait. After startup and any live-publish coordination, use one threadCloseTimeoutMs budget for settling the cancelled turn and waiting on session close. Start close exactly once even when the budget is exhausted. Seal the writer and fence late turn callbacks and writes. Keep the separate log-drain timeout and daemon halt semantics.

**Scope** — In: change src/thread/thread-job-run.ts and thread-event-writer.ts; extend test/unit/thread-event-writer.spec.ts, thread-job-run-hardening.spec.ts and thread-job-run-turns.spec.ts, retaining halt-safety controls. Out: normal RUN cancellation cutoff (US-006), changing thread protocol events, startup/live-publish coordination policy or log-drain timeout settings. Create no new files.

**Interface** — Retain the single startClose/startSessionClose owner and first close reason. Start the shared close deadline only after startup/live-publish coordination; turn settlement consumes that budget and close waits only its remainder. Even zero remaining time must initiate session.close once. A retained writer reference must refuse event, flush and callback writes after its terminal marker; clearing the run's writer reference alone is insufficient. Fence late turn completion from rearming timers, changing spend/journal or publishing another end. A timely turn's final transcript still precedes the single close marker. Halt stops writes and heartbeats and leaves a recoverable row without a terminal event.

**Verification** — Use real temporary stream files, real SQLite and manualClock, with held transcript finalizers and close promises; assert stream bytes and durable terminal state outside swallowed callbacks. Cover partial-budget settlement, timeout with a still-held finalizer, exactly-once close, timely finalization and halt during settlement. The separate log drain can complete immediately in the close-budget proof; dated lifecycle fixtures remain read-only.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given ready startup, held transcript finalization and an immediately completing log drain, when THREAD_CLOSE is delivered and the injected clock advances by threadCloseTimeoutMs, the run seals its stream while the finalizer remains held.

[integration] Given the same held-finalizer THREAD_CLOSE with ready startup and an immediately completing log drain, when the close budget expires, the journal job has non-null doneAt without requiring finalizer release.
[integration] Given the same held-finalizer THREAD_CLOSE, when the close budget expires with log drain complete, heartbeats stop.
[unit] Given turn settlement consumes part of threadCloseTimeoutMs and session.close remains held, finishRun waits only the remaining close budget.
[unit] Given settlement consumes part or all of the close budget, finishRun starts session.close exactly once.
[unit] Given a sealed thread stream, when the held finalizer is released and late callbacks write through a retained writer, the stream bytes stay fixed.
[unit] Given a sealed, completed thread run, when a held finalizer and late callbacks settle, its terminal event count stays fixed.
[unit] Given a sealed, completed thread run, when a held finalizer and late callbacks settle, its journal completion stays fixed.
[unit] Given timely turn settlement during close, the final transcript content precedes the single close marker.
[unit] When daemon halt occurs during turn settlement, the job remains recoverable without publishing a terminal event.

routing.reasoning: Agent-session lifecycle, shared deadlines and late writes cross asynchronous ownership boundaries; session handling uses strict isolated TDD.

userStories.title: Fence scheduled job insertion against project deletion
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Serialize fleet job creation with project soft deletion so a previously authorized schedule cannot insert into a deleted project.

**Motivation** — Project and repository removal can also leave jobs, stored files and search results inconsistent.

**Approach** — Finding 4. ScheduleTicker.dispatchFresh checks owner access before FleetJobsService.dispatch opens the job insertion transaction. Inside that transaction acquire a row lock on the live Project using a transaction-aware repository method, compatible with both soft-delete UPDATE paths. Decide liveness under the lock before creating the job or its dependent records. Keep the established handling for a refused dispatch and post-commit placement.

**Scope** — In: extend jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts, prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts and fleet-jobs.service.ts; update dispatch fixtures in fleet-jobs.service.spec.ts, fleet-jobs.audit.spec.ts and fleet-jobs.thread-handoff.spec.ts. Extend fleet-schedule-ticker.integration.spec.ts and retain project-deletion-quiesce.integration.spec.ts controls. Out: repository cleanup (US-009), bundle reconciliation (US-010), permission policy/catalog changes and changing the ticker's claim protocol. Create no new files.

**Interface** — Declare the project-liveness lock on IFleetJobRepository and implement it using the active transaction-aware Prisma client. The lock must conflict with a non-key deletedAt UPDATE from both ID and slug deletion; FOR KEY SHARE is insufficient. Refuse a missing/deleted project within the insertion transaction before job, links, event, activity or audit insertion. Preserve ScheduleTicker's owner authorization, error classification and no enclosing transaction around dispatch, plus post-commit live publication/placement and deletion-listener quiescence of queued jobs.

**Verification** — The reviewed database controls established separate sides of this race, not its interleaving. Add deterministic two-connection PostgreSQL tests: pause after owner authorization, delete through the application and resume with no runner attached; separately pause after the locked live-project read, start application deletion on another connection, observe PostgreSQL lock waiting, then release insertion and verify listener cancellation. Keep a live-project authorized-owner success control and two-ticker occurrence race. Run DB regressions on isolated test PostgreSQL outside the sandbox using the shared DB gate; skipped controls are not verification.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given disposable PostgreSQL with no runner attached and a due tick paused after successful owner authorization, when application soft deletion commits before the tick resumes, a fresh database read finds zero jobs for that schedule.
[integration] Given the same delete-before-insert interleaving with no runner attached, when the tick resumes, no assignment command exists for that schedule's dispatch.

[integration] Given an authorized insert paused after its in-transaction live-project read, when application soft deletion starts on a second PostgreSQL connection, PostgreSQL lock-wait observation establishes that deletion waits for insertion.
[integration] Given deletion waiting for the authorized insert, when insertion is released and deletion commits, the deletion listener cancels the queued job.
[integration] Given a live project and authorized schedule owner, when a due tick runs, it creates exactly one job, including when two tickers race to claim the same occurrence.

routing.reasoning: Three existing production files can reuse the repository/ALS row-lock pattern without new architecture; two-connection race tests and the authorization/liveness boundary still require strict isolated TDD.

userStories.title: Retain cleanup targets across fleet repository deletion
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve terminal-job file cleanup work durably before repository cascades erase its discovery metadata.

**Motivation** — Project and repository removal can also leave jobs, stored files and search results inconsistent.

**Approach** — Finding 5. FleetReposService.remove locks the repository, rejects unfinished jobs, then deletes it. Cascades erase the only lookup for logs and bundles. Capture terminal job IDs, lease-epoch bounds, finished times and exact bundle keys in durable cleanup records in the same transaction, before the cascade. Keep those records independent of the deleted parents. Extend the existing retention pass to consume eligible records using its cutoff and store methods. Use bounded batches, retry partial failures idempotently and acknowledge only after all targeted deletions succeed. Keep the existing retention setting and schedule.

**Scope** — In: add the independent Prisma cleanup model and migration; extend fleet-repos.service.ts, repos/domain/fleet-repo.domain.ts and prisma-fleet-repo.repository.ts for transactional capture; extend logs/domain/log-retention.domain.ts, prisma-log-retention.repository.ts and fleet-log-retention.processor.ts for due-work consumption. Out: project dispatch fencing (US-008), request-time bundle reconciliation (US-010), search ranking (US-011). userStories.title: Reconcile a stored bundle after metadata failure
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reconcile this upload attempt after metadata transaction failure without deleting committed or uncertain bundle bytes.

**Motivation** — Project and repository removal can also leave jobs, stored files and search results inconsistent.

**Approach** — Finding 6. BundleService.upload generates a unique attempt key, writes bytes, then uses a transaction to fence and record that attempt. Known rejections already delete the new object. Handle a thrown transactional error as well. After the transaction settles, use a fresh primary database read for this job, bundle kind and epoch. Delete only an attempt known to be unreferenced. If the commit is uncertain and the read itself fails, retain the bytes, emit a recoverable diagnostic identifying the attempt, and propagate the original failure. This story covers request-time reconciliation.

For bundle reconciliation, a primary read must observe the settled metadata transaction. If an acknowledgement was lost and its commit could still be running, serialize the verification with the same job-row lock in a fresh transaction before reading the artifact pointer. An inconclusive verification preserves the bytes. Per-attempt keys are unique, so subsequent upload attempts cannot reclaim an old key. The exception path only cleans up its own attempt.

**Scope** — In: extend artifacts/bundle.service.ts, bundle.service.spec.ts and test/integration/fleet/fleet-bundles.integration.spec.ts. Out: durable retired-job cleanup (US-009), changes to the ArtifactStore contract, and changes to holder fencing, normal ingest or log fallback behavior. Also out: A retrospective scan or deletion of files orphaned before the cleanup records exist. Changes to the public approval wire format, permission catalog or fleet protocol. Create no new files.

**Interface** — Reuse IFleetJobRepository.lockById/findArtifact and ArtifactStore.delete. Leave the failed metadata transaction scope before verification; in a fresh primary transaction acquire the same job-row lock used to record metadata and read the pointer for (jobId, 'bundle', leaseEpoch). Retain an attempt referenced by durable metadata or one whose status cannot be established. Delete only this attempt's confirmed orphan key, never the previous good or another attempt's key. Verification or deletion errors produce an identifying recoverable diagnostic without replacing the original request error. Maintain known rejection cleanup, successful replacement behavior and per-attempt random keys.

**Verification** — Use actual disk-store bytes for replacement rollback, two-connection lost-ack reconciliation and a successful new-key retry. Hold the recording transaction's job lock after it points at the new key, observe the verification transaction waiting with bytes present, commit and verify the original error still propagates with readable committed bytes. Inject verification-read and orphan-delete errors in unit tests. Dated bundle-cleanup fixtures are read-only.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given replacement bundle bytes were written but metadata transaction fails before recording them and the database is reachable, the new attempt file is removed.
[integration] Given the same pre-record metadata failure, the upload request fails with the original transaction error.
[integration] Given the same pre-record metadata failure after replacement bytes were written, the previous bundle row and its bytes remain readable.

[integration] Given a lost commit acknowledgement and a recording transaction holding the job-row lock after pointing at the new attempt, when reconciliation starts on a second PostgreSQL connection, lock-wait observation establishes that verification waits for that lock while the bytes remain present.
[integration] Given the lost-ack recording transaction commits after verification waits, the request reports its original error.
[integration] Given the lost-ack recording transaction commits after verification waits, the recorded bundle remains readable.
[unit] Given an uncertain commit and a failed verification read, BundleService.upload retains the attempt bytes.
[unit] Given an uncertain commit and a failed verification read, the recoverable diagnostic identifies the attempt key.
[unit] Given an uncertain commit and a failed verification read, the transaction error remains the request error.
[unit] Given a confirmed orphan whose deletion fails, an identifying diagnostic is emitted without masking the original transaction failure.
[integration] Given a failed upload is retried with a new key, a successful retry has readable bytes matching its durable metadata.
[integration] Given the successful retry uses a new key, cleanup for the failed attempt cannot remove that successful key.

routing.reasoning: Ambiguous commit reconciliation crosses database and disk durability; an incorrect primary-read or lock boundary can irreversibly delete committed bytes.

modifiedFiles.reason: reconcile the attempt outside the failed transaction and preserve the original error.
inject transaction, verification-read and delete errors.

userStories.title: Rank knowledge candidates from registered repositories
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Restrict lexical and vector candidate retrieval to eligible registered project repositories before either row cap.

**Motivation** — Project and repository removal can also leave jobs, stored files and search results inconsistent.

**Approach** — Finding 7. KnowledgeSearchService.search currently chooses bounded lexical and vector candidates before listProjectRepos is consulted. Obtain the project registry first and apply the registered repo IDs, intersected with any requested repo, inside both storage predicates before either leg's row cap. Preserve project partitioning, source selection, embedded-row constraints, path-prefix behavior, rank fusion, outcome job visibility, lexical-only mode and the existing meaning of empty. Empty eligibility must never broaden a query.

**Scope** — In: modify knowledge-search.service.ts, knowledge-search.service.spec.ts and test/integration/fleet/knowledge-store.integration.spec.ts. Verify shared service behavior consumed by the REST route and assistant tool. Out: retired-file cleanup (US-009), deleting retired Lance chunks instead of filtering, changing callers' public contracts. Also out: Expansion of the existing project-repository enumeration limit. US-011 takes eligible repository IDs from the current bounded listProjectRepos result. Create no new files.

**Interface** — Keep KnowledgeSearchQuery/KnowledgeSearchResult and KnowledgeChunkStore lexical/vector interfaces. Read the bounded registry first, intersect optional repoId, and pass the same eligible set into both source predicates before where/limit retrieval. An empty intersection produces zero eligible hits, never an omitted filter. Preserve docs/outcomes/all namespaces, provider != 'none' on the vector leg, project_<projectId> partitioning, post-leg path-prefix handling, reciprocal rank fusion, job visibility and final limits. Keep empty tied to stored rows of the requested source, not zero hits or zero eligible repositories; retain lexical fallback when embedding fails. The REST unknown owner/name response remains knowledge.repoNotFound.

**Verification** — Extend service-boundary tests for empty, foreign, retired and live explicit repos and all sources/visibility controls. Use real temporary LanceDB to place the only live lexical match below 50 higher-ranked retired rows; separately use controlled embeddings with no lexical query match to prove the live vector candidate survives retired candidates. Restore and close all native-store resources. Dated search-ranking fixtures are read-only references.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given one matching live document below 50 higher-ranked retired documents, project-wide lexical-only search returns the live document.
[integration] Given one matching live document below 50 higher-ranked retired documents, project-wide lexical-only search returns zero retired hits.

[integration] Given controlled embeddings and real LanceDB with the only live vector match below retired candidates and no lexical query match, vector-enabled KnowledgeSearchService.search returns the live document.
[unit] Given an empty project registry, KnowledgeSearchService.search returns zero eligible hits.
[unit] Given an explicit retired repoId, KnowledgeSearchService.search returns zero eligible hits.
[unit] Given an explicit repoId belonging to another project, KnowledgeSearchService.search returns zero eligible hits.
[unit] Given an explicit live registered repoId, KnowledgeSearchService.search restricts both lexical and vector legs to that repository.

[unit] Given an unknown owner/name repository selector, ProjectKnowledgeController.search throws NotFoundAppException for knowledge.repoNotFound, retaining the REST route's existing not-found response.

[unit] Given matching docs and accessible outcomes in registered repositories and a limit large enough to include both, KnowledgeSearchService.search returns only hits with source 'repo' for docs, only source 'outcome' for outcomes, and both source families for all, preserving existing source filtering.

[unit] Given registered repositories and a pathPrefix, KnowledgeSearchService.search returns only repository-document hits whose path starts with that prefix and no outcome hits, preserving existing path-prefix filtering for docs, outcomes and all.
[unit] Given registered repositories with outcome candidates for inaccessible jobs, KnowledgeSearchService.search returns no outcome hit for a job omitted by describeJobs.
[unit] Given registered repositories with lexical matches and an embedding failure, KnowledgeSearchService.search returns those lexical hits with lexicalOnly true, retaining lexical fallback.

[unit] Given docs, outcomes or all searches, including when eligible repositories yield no hits, KnowledgeSearchService.search returns empty true exactly when the project's table has no stored rows of the requested source family (repo for docs, outcome for outcomes, either for all), keeping empty keyed to stored source rows rather than eligible-hit count.

routing.reasoning: Hybrid native-store ranking must preserve source semantics and project/job visibility while moving eligibility before truncation; access-scope correctness invokes the security override.

modifiedFiles.reason: scope both rank inputs to project-registered repositories before truncating candidates.
cover eligibility, mode and project scope controls.
exercise the search service with real LanceDB ordering and constraints.

analysis:
Brownfield scope and evidence
Resolve only findings 4–14 from docs/20261125-review-whole-repo.md in one feature and PR, with the eleven prescribed owning stories. The review identifies historical observations at 7e2342791 and the supplied spec identifies integration checks at abae5e5b5; this analysis reads the current checkout rather than claiming to reproduce those commits. Findings 4–14 are described at docs/20261125-review-whole-repo.md:31–117. The historical fixtures under docs/review-evidence/20261125 assert the old failures and are read-only references, not regression tests to update. The feature is done when package regressions demonstrate each action, race, shutdown boundary, cleanup lifecycle and search result specified below, including deterministic PostgreSQL interleavings rather than only the old separate database controls. No implementation or tests were executed while drafting this PRD. Codebase-memory MCP and shell/test execution tools are not exposed in this session; navigation used direct reads and targeted text searches.

Architecture and rules
Despite the automated context labeling web as Next.js, the app is Nuxt 4 SSR with Vue, hand-written Nuxt composables and Jest/Playwright (.nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:11–32). Browser /api calls proxy through Nuxt; SSR uses internal API addressing and forwarded request cookies. apps/web/composables/useApi.ts:213–275 contains this transport and apps/web/composables/useApi.ts:276–299 contains the existing one-refresh retry. Preserve SSR headers, language, cookie forwarding and retry behavior; do not introduce a generated web client or generic interception of every 202. All new feedback must use both apps/web/i18n/locales/en.json and zh.json. Reuse existing UI primitives, ErrorState/LoadingState, permission composables and semantic tokens. These are workflow corrections, not a navigation/token/board redesign. API is NestJS on Fastify with Prisma 7 and Vitest, not bare Fastify. Runner is Bun-only ESM with real bun:sqlite journals and injected clocks/executor/session seams. API repository access must remain behind existing domain interfaces/tokens; extend the existing module-private repositories rather than introducing cross-module Prisma access. .nax/rules/api-data.md:19–116 defines repository → service → public layering, transaction-aware PrismaService.client and txManager.run; do not bypass ALS with a cached raw client or explicit tx parameters. Read .nax/rules/nathapp-packages.md and use nathapp-nestjs-docs when available before implementing API platform changes. Use generated Prisma types from src/generated/prisma/client, not @prisma/client. .nax/rules/api-auth.md:11–30 requires permission keys, not role claims. API state changes still go through JobTransitionsService; publish live events and invoke placement after commit. No approval DTO, permission-catalog, fleet-protocol or generated CLI changes are needed.

Shared design instructions (verbatim)
Each story below names the current producer, the consuming entry point, the changed behavior and the checks at their boundary. Use the existing project rules in `.nax/rules/`, including the permission-key, repository, transaction, test-isolation and web i18n rules. Regression tests belong in package test suites. The dated review fixtures assert historical behavior and are read-only references.
For the three approval-gated web calls, use the existing unwrapped approval summary. Check the operation's permission key, pending status and request ID, following the existing fleet dispatch UI. A pending transcript message also has a pending status. A queued reindex also has HTTP status 202. Neither alone identifies an approval.
For bundle reconciliation, a primary read must observe the settled metadata transaction. If an acknowledgement was lost and its commit could still be running, serialize the verification with the same job-row lock in a fresh transaction before reading the artifact pointer. An inconclusive verification preserves the bytes. Per-attempt keys are unique, so subsequent upload attempts cannot reclaim an old key. The exception path only cleans up its own attempt.

US-001 / finding 10: scoped approval outcomes
The producer apps/api/src/approvals/route/approval-gated.decorator.ts:24–34 replies 202 with JsonResponse.Ok(ApprovalRequestSummaryDto.from(...)), not a special outer pending marker. The unwrapped type already exists at apps/web/lib/approval-requests.ts:42–65. The exact route keys are ticket.create (apps/api/src/tickets/tickets.controller.ts:173), fleet.job.cancel (apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.controller.ts:62), and thread.message.send (apps/api/src/fleet/threads/threads.controller.ts:300). apps/web/components/fleet/FleetJobOpenItems.vue:60–80 shows scoped permissionKey/status checks and returned request IDs for existing dispatch/ruling flows; mirror that behavior. apps/web/composables/useFleetJobs.ts:6–8 already unions dispatch with ApprovalRequestSummary, but cancel still promises FleetJobDto at line 78. apps/web/components/CreateTicketDialog.vue:132–140 ignores the create response, emits created, closes and resets. apps/web/pages/[project]/fleet/jobs/[id]/index.vue:239–247 applies the cancel result as a job before its success toast; preserveJobLabels must still be used for executed replies. apps/web/lib/thread-controller.ts:48–52 defines ThreadActionResult; send at line 225 creates a pending optimistic message and line 252 destructures an executed { message } unconditionally. apps/web/components/fleet/threads/ThreadComposer.vue:68–77 clears equal submitted drafts when result.ok, with protection for newer edits; preserve that protection and distinguish execution from approval pending. Both project and workspace page onSend adapters forward that action result; pending is not an error toast and must not enter closing/transport retry loops. Modify useApi.ts only to enable scoped result discrimination, useFleetJobs.ts, CreateTicketDialog.vue, thread-controller.ts, ThreadComposer.vue and both detail pages plus locales. Extend existing tests/components/CreateTicketDialog.spec.ts, tests/pages/fleet-job-detail.spec.ts, tests/lib/thread-controller.spec.ts, tests/components/thread-composer.spec.ts, tests/pages/threads-detail-actions-page.spec.ts and tests/composables/useApi.spec.ts. The actions page already mounts the real composer at apps/web/tests/pages/threads-detail-actions-page.spec.ts:68; use it to observe feedback and editable drafts.

US-002 / finding 11: ready-boundary reconciliation
Both adapters initially load then subscribe: apps/web/composables/useThread.ts:41–50 and useWorkspaceThread.ts:72–81. apps/web/lib/thread-event-stream.ts:123–132 currently calls onResync at reopen after hadError, while ready only sets live; move catch-up to one ready notification per connected stream, including native EventSource reconnects, without double-fetching on open plus ready. Retain dedupe, tri-state refreshAuth, backoff and stopped checks at thread-event-stream.ts:70–117. apps/web/lib/thread-controller.ts:114–137 performs unversioned detail/message reads; event, poll and resync handlers at lines 145–194 use fire-and-forget reads, currently without rejection handling. Responses can arrive after newer reads, live deltas or stop. Protect response order and same-message revisions, not just the highest message seq: a delta appends to a message without changing seq. apps/web/lib/thread-view.ts:19–48 preserves longer content only when both versions are streaming, so a late pending/streaming snapshot can still regress a terminal state or content. The injected controller harness at apps/web/tests/lib/thread-controller.spec.ts:66–95 captures handlers and timers and can hold promises deterministically. US-003 / finding 12: project deep-link feedback
apps/web/composables/useThread.ts:44–48 suppresses initial failures and exposes only ThreadController. The workspace adapter's loadFailed/loadThread contract at apps/web/composables/useWorkspaceThread.ts:22–28 and :54–68 is the existing recovery pattern. Its page prioritizes loaded detail, then failure, then loading at apps/web/pages/threads/[id].vue:93–131. US-004 / finding 13: project list pagination
apps/web/composables/useThreads.ts:35–52 has a generation counter but requests only { status, size: '100' }. apps/web/composables/useWorkspaceThreads.ts:29–108 already provides current, hasNext, loadingMore and loadMore; it advances the page only after a successful current-generation response. Mirror its contract and selected-status preservation while guarding page-one reloads as well as status changes. apps/web/pages/[project]/threads/index.vue:22–41 has an additional page-load token covering members.load; do not replace it with only the composable generation. Its template at lines 83–85 has no pagination control. Add load-more and failure feedback retaining visible rows and the failed page. Extend tests/composables/useThreads.spec.ts (existing exact first-page query assertions at lines 36–60 and generation regressions thereafter) and tests/pages/threads-page.spec.ts; mirror workspace list/page patterns. Keep first-page query compatibility and reuse existing localized load-more/retry copy.

US-005 / finding 14: effective send access
apps/web/lib/thread-view.ts:80–105 takes ComposerViewer.isCreator before server sendRefusal and isTurnRunning. The project page already derives isCreator and useProjectPermissions at apps/web/pages/[project]/threads/[id].vue:43–49, but passes only isCreator at line 175. apps/web/lib/permissions.ts:37–42 defines has as any-row only and hasOwn as any-row OR .own; use has('thread.message.send') OR (isCreator AND hasOwn('thread.message.send')), never promote another creator's own-only grant. apps/web/composables/usePermissions.ts:94–100 supplies EMPTY_PERMISSIONS while pending or failed, including refresh. Pass the resolved reactive send decision into shared composerState, retaining server refusal and running-turn priority after the read-only decision. apps/web/pages/threads/[id].vue:123–127 must adapt its existing personal-owner decision, without importing project permission data for workspace composer access. Other thread controls continue to use their existing creator/requester/archive/mode rules. Extend tests/lib/thread-view.spec.ts, tests/pages/threads-detail-page.spec.ts and workspace-thread-detail-page.spec.ts. Update the real-composer creator fixture in threads-detail-actions-page.spec.ts with thread.message.send.own alongside thread.archive, keeping typing, submission and refusal-toast assertions.

US-006 / finding 8: cancellation linearization
apps/runner/src/supervisor/job-run.ts:184–194 accepts any nonterminal row, including UPLOADING. finish at line 576 judges before draining, awaits logs at line 647, transitions UPLOADING at line 649 and later emits the earlier verdict at line 672. Establish one synchronous/journal-atomic decision after the drain that checks durable RUN cancellation and advances RUNNING → UPLOADING; avoid an await between the last check and transition. Journal.tx exists at apps/runner/src/journal/journal.ts:79 and writes are durable before observers/acks. requestCancel must use the same RUN cutoff and reject new post-cutoff requests. apps/runner/src/supervisor/supervisor.ts:155–169 discards the active run's boolean and returns ok even for journal-only terminal rows; propagate the decision and apply it to journal-only RUN recovery. apps/runner/src/supervisor/command-handler.ts:180–182 translates cancel into acknowledgements, while :85–106 replays recorded command outcomes before applying anything anew; preserve replay identity and don't reevaluate a previously handled CANCEL by current job state. Cancellation during held logs wins over a previously computed successful RUN verdict and persists through restart. Do not generalize RUN result precedence to CONFIG: finishConfig is separate at job-run.ts:349 and src/supervisor/job-run-config.spec.ts has command-specific authoritative-result controls. Extend job-run.spec.ts, supervisor.spec.ts and command-handler.spec.ts using real Journal, FakeExecutor, FakeLogShipping and fakeTime; command-handler.spec.ts:423 already controls held versus unknown jobs. Maintain lease epochs, one terminal event, upload fencing, PLAN/REVIEW/FIX behavior and thread paths.

US-007 / finding 9: one close budget and late-write fencing
apps/runner/src/thread/thread-job-run.ts:975–1008 awaits startup and livePublish, cancels the turn, waits turnSettled without a deadline, then starts closeHeldSession. closeHeldSession at :710–714 clears the session, while startSessionClose at :1191–1197 owns the exactly-once close promise and awaitSessionClose at :1221–1234 starts a fresh full timeout. The hardening harness injects manualClock, real files, SQLite and session behavior at apps/runner/test/unit/thread-job-run-hardening.spec.ts:27–69, enabling held finalizer/close budgets without real-time sleeps or paid agents.

US-008 / finding 4: live-project insertion fence
apps/api/src/fleet/schedules/schedule-ticker.ts:147–173 authorizes owner access outside dispatch and intentionally has no transaction around dispatch. Its onDispatchError at :193–218 preserves template-invalid refusal and post-commit-side-effect handling. apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.ts:90–128 resolves repo, tickets, pin, budget and snapshots before opening insertion; :130–177 inserts job, links, events, activity and audit in txManager.run, and :186–196 publishes and places after commit. Decide live state inside the same insert transaction before job or dependent writes and before any thread lock/insert effects. The repo's ALS client is already used at apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts:94–97; lockById at :249–252 shows the row-lock pattern. Both application delete paths must conflict with this boundary: apps/api/src/projects/projects.service.ts:251–284 calls ID-based and slug-based update methods under audited transactions, then announces deletion after commit at :295–300. apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/project-deletion-jobs.listener.ts:39–56 quiesces unstarted jobs after deletion, publishing after its own transaction; retain this opposite-order control. US-009 / finding 5: durable retired-job cleanup
apps/api/src/fleet/repos/fleet-repos.service.ts:669–681 locks FleetRepo, rejects unfinished jobs, then cascades deletion inside the same transaction as activity/audit. prisma-fleet-repo.repository.ts:313–319 uses ACTIVE_STATES and FOR UPDATE. FleetJob.repo and artifact/log relations cascade (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:1232, :1567, :1588), removing all current retention discovery pointers. apps/api/src/fleet/logs/prisma-log-retention.repository.ts:16–32 only discovers surviving terminal FleetJob rows with unexpired rows or log events, ordered by (finishedAt,id) in bounded pages. fleet-log-retention.processor.ts:36–47 uses the existing 04:45 cron and logRetentionDays setting; :56–75 walks RETENTION_BATCH=200 with a cursor that advances even after per-job failure, and :78–96 deletes log prefixes through selected epoch and exact artifact keys before expiring rows under lock. Introduce an independent cleanup model and the sole new authored file apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261219090000_fleet_retired_job_cleanup/migration.sql, including a due-work index and no historical rewrite/backfill. Capture stable terminal job ID, max lease epoch, finish time and exact bundle keys in the deletion transaction before cascade; records must have no cascading dependence on Project/FleetRepo/FleetJob. Persist capture through the repo domain/repository, not cross-module service Prisma calls. Extend log-retention.domain.ts, prisma-log-retention.repository.ts and the existing processor to cursor-page due records with the same cutoff and store APIs. Acknowledge only once every target delete succeeds; retries must tolerate absent files and not starve later records behind one persistent failure. Extend fleet-repos.service.spec.ts for capture/rollback and busy refusal, fleet-log-retention.processor.spec.ts for partial success/replay/progress and test/integration/fleet/fleet-log-retention.integration.spec.ts using actual repository DELETE, temporary disk files, worker restart and cutoff advance. US-010 / finding 6: request-time bundle reconciliation
apps/api/src/fleet/artifacts/bundle.service.ts:59–66 writes a server-generated randomUUID key per attempt. :71–98 re-locks the job, fences the holder/state, records artifact + ingest + activity + audit in a transaction. Only returned known rejections delete this attempt (:99–102); thrown transaction errors currently escape without reconciliation. Its success path schedules log fallback, kicks ingest and deletes the replaced key after commit (:104–125). Preserve all of these existing responsibilities. On thrown metadata failure, leave the failed transaction scope and start a fresh primary transaction, acquire that same job lock, then read the artifact pointer for this job/kind/epoch. A plain immediate read is unsafe for a lost-ack commit still running; the verification transaction must wait until its row lock settles. If pointer equals this key retain it; only a confirmed unreferenced own key can be deleted.
